It changes the strategy to start C, then D,D, classify opponents, defect all against always-C/always-D, and use forgiving TFT with endgame exploitation against conditional retaliators.

--- PART 3/7 ---
ORIGIN: NONE

STRATEGY: The parent is a strategy being revised against a population of 12 slots; the trace simulates probing with C/D/D and then defecting all against opponents whose first three actions are all C. It identifies slots 6, 9, and 11 as always-C and slot 5 as exploitative, then changes the plan to a hybrid that defects all if the opponent never defects but switches to TFT/forgiveness if the opponent defects.

STRATEGY: The parent is a TFT variant that cooperates when opponent has no defections and defects after opponent defections. The trace simulates candidate revisions against population slots (slot0, slot1, slot5, always-C, TFT-like) and computes round-by-round payoffs. It changes the probe/forgiveness rules (R2 defect probe, R3-R6 classification, forgiving TFT, endgame defection) to exploit always-C without triggering delayed retaliators.

STRATEGY: The parent (slot10) cooperates unless behind, defects if opponent defected last round, and never forgives. The trace simulates it against slot1, always-C, slot0, TFT, and slot5, then designs a new probe-and-forgive strategy (C, then D on R2–R5, then forgiving TFT with endgame defection).
